top_problem: The reading layer's grid is nearly flawless, but the page around it is not composed. The wordmark rule bleeds only to the right. The right text margin is 3x the left. A 20.6 mm dead band sits under the subline. The soil band (15% of the page) reads as a dashed textile or water, not Iowa loam. So the boldest missing idea is still a true fusion: the level Iowa horizon and the agave should be one structural line that the list itself is set against, not a stock dark-ground agave vignette that ref-02 panel 1 already does better.
remove: Remove the clod and pebble ovals and the two broken horizon boundaries in the loam. At actual size they read as bubbles and waterlines, which undercuts the 'soil, not sea' fix and adds a fifth salient region.
fixes: Balance the page frame: stop the wordmark horizon rule at the same 64 px safe edge on the right (or bleed it on both sides) so the top rule does not make the only asymmetric margin.

Pull the subline-to-sections gap from 78 px down to 48-56 px (on the 8 px grid), and use the gained space to raise the soil line so column 1's end and the soil line share a deliberate 32 px section-gap relation.

Set the spirits price the same 15 px hop after the name and move POUR into the description line ('Blanco tequila · pour'), so all 14 rows share one inline price rhythm and '18' cannot read as a pour size.
Re-clamp the rosette so every leaf edge clears text by at least 6 mm (the Blanco '12' is at 4.8 mm now), and turn the left leaf tip away from the Dry Cider row.

Restore dominance by enlarging the rosette (S ~780 on the I5 table) or deepening the heart shading so primary area returns to ≥5% and primary-to-secondary to ≥15, then fix the phone leading so its row tops land on mod-8.

measurements.margins: Text sits 64 px from the left and 176 px from the right (column 2 ends at 640). The art bleeds right and bottom, so the page is asymmetric by design. The empty band from 162 to 240 px (about 21 mm) between the subtitle and the first H2 does no work.

measurements.squint: 5 salient regions. The primary covers 2.86% of the page, down from 5.53%, and primary-to-secondary is 4.56, down from 22.37. This is a regression and focal dominance is weak.
measurements.colour_match: proposal.md has no colour-match figures. The only accent figure is accent_area_pct 0.21 from visual_tests, so I could not verify the accent's colour match.
measurements.reference_compared: I opened ref-05 (The Greenhouse) only. That board has one art-directed world with type and image fused. I8 is a clean list set beside a separate drawing.

remove: The 23 clod and pebble ovals in the loam band. At actual size they read as bubbles, which pushes the soil back toward water, the very reading the avoid-list forbids, and they add a third mark type (dash, stipple, oval) to a band that should be quiet.
top_problem: The wordmark is a widely tracked, spa-weight Cormorant 'C A N T I N A' (a placeholder word) that could head a candle shop or a day spa. Its only link to the concept is the horizon rule, which cuts through the serif feet instead of carrying them. The boldest missing idea is display type that is itself the fusion: letterforms cut or engraved in the agave's own line grammar standing on the Iowa soil line, so that the wordmark, not the plant, is the entry point.
fixes: Replace the spa-tracked Cormorant wordmark with a display treatment that shares the agave's engraved hatch or has a Mexican letter-painting (rotulo) structure, tighten the tracking to about 0.08-0.12em so it reads as a word, and set the rule 2-4 px below the baseline (or knock it out around the letters) so it no longer runs through the serif feet.

Fix the hierarchy inversion: take the H2s to at least 18-20 px, or keep 14.5 px and drop the item names to 15 px, so section heads outrank items in size as well as colour, and cut the subtitle's repeated 'Cantina' (for example 'Cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa').

Rebuild focal order so the wordmark and rosette form one dominant group (squint primary above 5% and ratio above 10): scale the rosette back toward S 780 with I5's heavy heart shading, and close the dead 78 px band under the subtitle by tying the H2 row to the grid step directly below the header.

Put the phone on the 8 px grid (18 px name leading becomes 16 or 24, and 18 px description leading becomes 16 or 24), and make the Margarita's serve label match the others (drop the period after 'OVER FRESH ICE' and set the tasting note on its own line in sentence case).

Give the spirits and wine descriptions real lines, or suppress the tautologies ('Blanco Tequila / Blanco tequila', 'Cognac VSOP / VSOP Cognac'): typographically they are dead second lines that break the name-description rhythm, and at 7.5 pt the reversed caps serve labels need either 11 px or ivory at full strength for dim-bar reading.

remove: Remove the clod and pebble ovals, and with them the C-horizon stipple band. At 1:1 the ovals read as bubbles, so the soil turns into aquarium gravel or water, the very thing the avoid-list forbids. They also add a second drawing grammar under the engraved agave.
top_problem: The Iowa half of the thesis never shows up. The soil band is a grey dash-and-stipple pattern with bubble-like ovals that reads as water or static, not Iowa loam. Without it, this is a well-drawn sage agave that any agave bar anywhere could use. It fails the substitution test, and the placeholder CANTINA wordmark makes it more generic still. The missing bold idea is a soil or ground plane that is unmistakably Iowa: for example, the agave's roots and horizon become the gridded section lines of an Iowa survey or plat, drawn in the same single-weight engraved line as the leaves.
fixes: Redraw the soil in the agave's own engraved line: horizontal hatch with the same stroke weight and modulation as the leaves, in sage, and delete the dashes, stipple and ovals. Then one grammar covers the whole art and the ground cannot read as water.

Give Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP the same 15 px price hop as every other row, and move POUR to the H3 line ('AGAVE · POUR') or to after the price, so the whole menu has one inline price rhythm instead of 15 px on some rows and 52 px on others.

Recover focal dominance (primary 2.86% / ratio 4.56 now): add I5's heavier heart shading to the rosette or scale S up toward 720. The agave must clearly outweigh the wordmark at thumbnail size, not tie with it.

Close the 77 px dead band between the subline and the section heads (to about 40 px) and give the space back to the bottom so col 1 does not crowd the soil line. Or balance the column ends by moving the 160 px difference into a quiet zone above the rosette.
Set prices in tabular lining figures and check that '11', '7' and '8' align optically; replace the placeholder CANTINA with the real name before any further scoring of criterion 15.

measurements.wordmark_contrast_verified: The rule is excluded because it sits at css y 117.8-118.7, and the crop stops at y 114. Letter ink #9CC3B5 on ground #1B1510 gives 9.37:1, which confirms the proposal. The 1.00 reading is caused by the rule, not the letters.

column_ends_css_px.note: The agave fills the gap, so the art is doing a job there.

measurements.dead_space: There is a 78 css px (about 21 mm) empty band between the sub-line (ends at 162) and the first H2 (240). It does no framing or grouping work. The soil line sits 32 px below the end of col 1.
measurements.inks: Umber ground, cream text, sage art and wordmark, terracotta H2, plus a fifth muted sage in the soil. Four or five inks where the brief allows 2-3.

remove: The clod and pebble ovals in the B/C horizons. At actual size they read as bubbles, so the soil turns into water, which is exactly what the avoid-list forbids. They add a second drawing grammar (closed ovals) to a line-engraving system.
top_problem: The big idea, Mexico growing out of Iowa, is only in the proposal's caption. Without it, the page is an engraved agave on a dark ground, which is ref-02 panel 1 redrawn. The Iowa half is a band of dashes and stipple that reads as gravel, rain or water, not as prairie loam. It fails the substitution test: any cantina in the country could print this page. Missing boldest idea: make the Iowa half as unmistakable as the agave, for example a flat, ruled Johnson County horizon (a section-line field grid or a corn-row perspective vanishing to the horizon rule) that the agave's roots visibly break into, drawn in the same line weight as the leaves.
fixes: Replace the dash/stipple/oval soil with one Iowa signifier drawn in the leaf engraving's own grammar (parallel hatch, same stroke weight and modulation), such as ruled furrows in shallow perspective. Grain and agave should share one illustration family and the fusion should be readable without a caption (criteria 15 and 16).

Redraw the front-right leaf and the long left leaf. The broad, rounded front-right leaf still reads as a bulb, artichoke or lotus, and the long left one as a fin. Give every leaf the lanceolate, tapering, rigid spike of Agave americana, with one stroke weight; this is also the cheap way to bring the squint dominance (primary 2.86%, ratio 4.56) back up without enlarging S.

Close the 21 mm dead band under the sub-line: move the lists up 32-40 px, or drop the wordmark's horizon rule to the list's top edge so the rule frames the list. The rule then echoes the soil line as a deliberate pair of horizons, the list sits between them, and the gap becomes framing space (criteria 6 and 5).
Cut to three inks. Draw the soil in the same sage as the leaves at reduced line density instead of adding a fifth muted tone, so terracotta stays the only accent (criteria 4 and 16).

Separate the inline serve labels (COUPE, OVER FRESH ICE, POUR) from the H3 subheads: set them in italic lowercase of the text serif, or at least one step lighter. At present, tracked sans caps carry two hierarchy levels, and 7.5 pt reversed caps are borderline in a dim bar (criteria 2 and environmental legibility). Also finish the phone 8 px grid.

top_problem: On the phone the concept falls apart. The horizon rule that the thesis says the wordmark 'stands on' is missing, the agave is cut back to 31% leaf length into glassy blue-green shards pushed against the right edge, and the loam is a 190 px textile strip under the last item. Print and phone read as two different menus. The boldest missing idea: the soil line is the menu's one structural horizon. On print and on phone, the list and the wordmark should both rest on it, so the agave grows out of the same line the type stands on and does not sit beside it.
remove: The clod and pebble ovals, and with them the B/C horizon stipple. Keep a single thin dashed A-horizon band. Right now the loam is a second illustration grammar (dash/stipple/ovals against the agave's modulated engraving) and at thumbnail size reads as woven fabric or water.
fixes: Phone: raise the serve and POUR labels from 10 px tracked caps to at least 12 px (about 11 pt) in small caps or italic lowercase. 10 px reversed grey caps fail the dim-bar environmental gate, and 'OVER A LARGE CUBE' and 'POUR' are essential serve facts.

Phone: bring back the wordmark's horizon rule and give the rosette its own full-width band below Spirits instead of clamping leaves to 0.31 beside the text. On a 390-wide single column the plant has to grow under the list, not squeeze into a 6 mm corridor next to it.

Put the phone on the 8 px grid (18 px leading becomes 16 or 24) so all 14 row tops land mod8=0 like print, and treat the spirits price hop the same way everywhere. The POUR label pushes those rows to 52 px gaps against 15 px for every other row: set 'pour' after the price or in the description line.

Print: close the 21 mm dead band between the subline and COCKTAILS, and balance the columns (42 mm end difference). Moving Spirits' Brandy sub-block, or adding space before the soil line under column 1, would let both columns end on one line above the soil.

Redraw the large front-right leaves with a narrower lanceolate outline and a heavier heart shade. At thumbnail they still read as an onion or lotus bulb, and the squint primary/secondary ratio fell from 22.4 to 4.6, so the agave no longer clearly dominates the wordmark.

lens: Every item and price checked against build/draft_doc.json (14 items, 4 sections), plus side-rail and tagline copy and section flow for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: Every price matches and nothing is invented, but the non-cocktail half of the menu reads as placeholder copy. 'Blanco tequila', 'Añejo tequila' and 'VSOP Cognac' just repeat the item names. 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' give no grape or region. The beers have a style but no ABV. At an agave-led Mexican bar, the Spirits section is the weakest and least prominent block on the page. The missing beer ABV, wine region and spirit brand data is Rob's open data gap, not the designer's fault, and proposal.md flags it correctly.
problems: Prices: all 14 match the draft exactly (Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18). No item is dropped or invented. Every price sits inline, about 15 px from its name (4% eye travel), so the association is clear.

The garnishes and serve facts (lime wheel, lime coin, orange peel, cocktail cherry, coupe, over fresh ice, over a large cube) are not in the draft. build.py's RV and SERVE tables trace them to phg.recipe_versions ids (f06abb74, 14d45e57, 7095fd3d, 9fb77eaa). I accept the source; the Accuracy reviewer should confirm it. The Manhattan correctly leaves out aromatic bitters (public_components aromatic-bitters:false).

The spirit descriptions repeat their names ('Blanco tequila' under Blanco Tequila, 'Añejo tequila' under Añejo Tequila, 'VSOP Cognac' under Cognac VSOP), which adds nothing. The beer lines are close to repeats too ('Hop-forward draft IPA' sits under a 'De barril · Draft' subhead).

Known data gap, Rob's to fill and not the designer's fault: beer brewery and ABV; cider producer, ABV and format; wine producer, region and vintage; tequila brand and añejo age; Cognac house; pour sizes. It is flagged item by item in proposal.md's missing_ingredients table. Until it is filled, criterion 8 cannot go past the mid-60s.

Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Espumoso · Sparkling' with no GLASS label. The 'Por copa · By the glass' label only covers Malbec and Pinot Grigio, so the sparkling price is ambiguous. It is flagged, but it is not resolved on the page.

Serve labels are inconsistent. The spirits carry a POUR label, but wine and beer have no serve label. The cocktails mix glassware (COUPE) with ice method (OVER FRESH ICE, OVER A LARGE CUBE), so the small-caps label means two different things.

The bilingual subhead system breaks in Spirits. Every other subhead is Spanish · English ('Clásicos · Classics', 'De barril · Draft', 'Sidra · Cider'), but 'AGAVE' and 'BRANDY' are English only, in the section a Mexican venue should own.

Reading path: the wordmark gives one clear entry, then Cocktails is a strong start. After that, column 1 (Cocktails, Beer & Cider) runs 160 px longer than column 2 (Wine, Spirits). Agave spirits come last, small, and crowded by the rosette leaves. For this venue type the tequila list deserves more than end-of-page placement. The draft has Cider as its own section; merging it into 'Beer & Cider' is acceptable, but the proposal does not note it.
Only the Margarita keeps a tasting note ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). The other 13 items are bare lists, so the descriptions do not share one voice.

The wordmark 'CANTINA' is a placeholder, not the venue's name (the proposal admits this). The rail line 'Cantina & cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' states no item fact, so it is allowed under the gate, but a placeholder name cannot be published.
fixes: Replace the spirit and wine name-echo descriptions with category facts from the draft's own taxonomy (for example 'Unaged 100% agave' only if sourced, otherwise 'Agave · blanco' plus a visible '[brand TBC]' flag), and populate grape/region/ABV/brand the moment Rob supplies the missing_ingredients data.

Add a serve label to Brut Rosé ('GLASS 13' or 'BOTTLE 13' once Rob confirms), and give wine and draft beer the same small-caps serve label as the spirits' POUR, so every price category states its unit.

Finish the bilingual system in Spirits ('Agave · Agave' and 'Brandy · Brandy' lose nothing, or use 'Destilados de agave · Agave'), and move Spirits or give Agave more weight so tequila is not the last and weakest block at a Mexican bar.
Split the cocktail serve labels into one consistent kind (glassware only, or method only), or give glass and ice their own clearly different tokens.

Balance the columns (move Sidra · Cider to column 2 under Wine, or re-pair sections) so the column ends are within one row, and replace the placeholder 'CANTINA' wordmark with the venue name before publishing.

top_problem: Half the menu has no real descriptions. The six wine and spirits lines just repeat the item name or its category ('Blanco tequila', 'Añejo tequila', 'VSOP Cognac', 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling rosé'), and beer and cider give a style but no ABV. The missing brand, region, vintage, ABV and pour-size data is a known gap: Rob has been asked for it and the designer flagged it correctly in the missing_ingredients table in proposal.md. It is not the designer's fault, but criterion 8 cannot score above the low 60s until Rob fills it.
problems: All 14 items and prices match build/draft_doc.json exactly (15/15/14/16, 7/8/7, 8, 12/11/13, 12/16/18). Nothing is invented, dropped or re-priced, and none of the taglines, side rails or props states an item fact. The only extra text is the generic subtitle 'Cantina & cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa'.

The Manhattan's aromatic bitters is correctly hidden (public_components aromatic-bitters:false). The garnishes (lime wheel, cocktail cherry, lime coin, orange peel) and serves come from the recipe versions, according to proposal.md. I could not check them against the database under this lens.

Spirits descriptions only repeat the name ('Blanco Tequila' / 'Blanco tequila'; 'Cognac VSOP' / 'VSOP Cognac'). They also drop the draft's word 'pour', which has moved into a separate POUR label. The line still gives the guest nothing new.
Wine has no region, producer or vintage (known gap). Brut Rosé 13 is unlabelled, and it is unclear whether that is a glass or a bottle price, even though it sits under 'Por Copa' only by proximity.
Beer and cider give a style but no ABV, brewery or pour size (known gap). A cocktail bar's beer list with no ABV falls short of the scorecard's 'style + ABV' requirement.

The serve labels follow three different rules. Manhattan and Daiquiri show a glass (COUPE). Margarita and Old Fashioned show ice ('OVER FRESH ICE.', with a stray full stop, and 'OVER A LARGE CUBE') but no glass. Spirits show a size word (POUR) with no measure.

The cocktail voice is uneven. Only the Margarita keeps a tasting line from the draft ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). The other three are bare ingredient lists, so the Brown Butter Old Fashioned, the signature item, has less character than the Margarita.

Criterion 5: the reading path is clear (Cocktails, then Beer & Cider, then Wine, then Spirits). Moving Cider from its own draft section into Beer is a sensible change, but proposal.md does not note it. The columns end 160 px apart (864 vs 704), and the lower third of the page is soil art with no content job. Spirits sits inside the agave's leaves, so it reads as an afterthought beside cocktails.
The Brown Butter Old Fashioned has no dairy or allergen note. It is flagged to Rob, but no footnote placeholder is printed.
The 'CANTINA' wordmark is a placeholder that stands in for the venue name. The draft's title is 'Bar menu'.
fixes: Once Rob supplies the data, rewrite each wine, beer, cider and spirits line from it: grape + region + producer for wine, style + ABV + brewery for beer and cider, brand + age + pour size for spirits. Until then, show a visible '[pending: ABV]'-style placeholder in the proof instead of lines that repeat the name.

Put one serve grammar on every cocktail (glass, then ice): 'rocks glass · large cube', 'coupe', and the Margarita's missing glass from its recipe version. Remove the stray full stop after 'OVER FRESH ICE'.
Label Brut Rosé's 13 as GLASS or BOTTLE once Rob confirms, and put the pour size (for example '1.5 oz') next to the spirits' POUR labels so the label carries information.

Either give every cocktail one short sourced tasting line, or drop 'Bright and citrus-forward' from the Margarita so all four cocktails share one voice. Keep the brown-butter dairy note as a footnote placeholder until Rob confirms.
Note the Cider-into-Beer merge in proposal.md, and even out the column ends so Spirits is not squeezed beside the art and reads as the equal of Cocktails.

lens: Flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The list reads in two tiers. The four cocktails get full spirit, modifier, garnish and serve lines. Every beer, wine and spirit gets a thin placeholder, and the three spirits only repeat their names ('Blanco tequila', 'Añejo tequila', 'VSOP Cognac'). The reading path is also broken: there is a dead band between the tagline and the first section, the two columns end 160 px apart, and the agave rosette at the bottom right is the heaviest mass on the page, so the eye is pulled away from the Spirits section, which is where a cantina's agave list should be the destination.
problems: Items and prices: all 13 draft items (doc.json) appear with matching prices: Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18. Nothing is invented or dropped. The draft's separate Cider section is now a 'Sidra · Cider' sub-group under Beer & Cider, which is acceptable.

Known data gap, not the designer's fault: beer ABV, brewery and pour size; wine region, producer and vintage; spirit brand, age and pour size are missing, and the designer flagged every one in proposal.md missing_ingredients. Until Rob supplies them, criterion 8 cannot pass for beer, wine or spirits.

Even with that gap, the non-cocktail descriptions are weak writing. The spirit lines repeat the item name. 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' say almost nothing. 'Toasty' (Amber Lager), 'Hop-forward' (IPA) and 'Bright and citrus-forward' (only on the Margarita) are tasting claims that need a source, or they should be dropped.

Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Espumoso · Sparkling', outside the 'Por copa · By the glass' heading, so the guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle price. The designer flagged this, but the layout leaves it ambiguous.

Price style is inconsistent: spirits insert a 'POUR' label between the name and the price, while wine, which is also sold by the glass, has no serve label on its rows. The inline prices do keep eye travel short.

Reading path: entry through the wordmark is clear, and the order (Cocktails, then Beer & Cider in column 1; Wine, then Spirits in column 2) follows the scorecard order. But there is about 150 px of dead space between the tagline and COCKTAILS. Column 2 stops about 300 px (display) above column 1. The rosette and the soil band then take the whole lower right, creating a second focal point that competes with the list. The designer's own squint test shows 5 salient regions.

For a Mexican cantina, the agave section is the smallest and last on the page (two tequilas, with Cognac under the same heading block). That under-weights the venue's signature category, though the list itself is Rob's content.
The Brown Butter Old Fashioned's dairy allergen (brown-butter fat-wash) is not confirmed. The designer flagged it correctly; it must be resolved before print.
Taglines checked: 'Cantina & cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' and the bilingual sub-heads are generic and state no item fact. Pass.
fixes: Once Rob supplies the missing data, rewrite each beer, wine and spirit line to its criterion-8 minimum (beer: style + ABV; wine: grape + region; spirits: type/age + brand). Until then, replace the lines that repeat the name with neutral, sourced serve facts, or leave them blank with the gap marked, rather than filler.
Put Brut Rosé under the 'Por copa · By the glass' heading, or label its price GLASS or BOTTLE once Rob confirms, and use one serve-label convention for both wine and spirits.
Close the dead band between the tagline and COCKTAILS and bring the two columns to within one row of each other, so the list reads as one block and not as a text slab floating above the art.

Give Spirits a stronger anchor in column 2 (for example, lead with 'Agave' as a titled sub-group and put Brandy in a smaller note), so the path ends on the cantina's signature category instead of drifting into the rosette.
Remove tasting claims with no source ('Bright and citrus-forward', 'Toasty', 'Hop-forward'), or get Rob to confirm them, so every description line is built only from known facts.

lens: Voice and consistency of descriptions, headings (including bilingual subheads) and venue copy; fit to a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The descriptions do not share one voice. The cocktails get dotted ingredient lists with small-caps serve tags. The Margarita alone carries a flavour line ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). Beer gets adjective-noun fragments. The spirit lines only repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila', 'Añejo tequila', 'VSOP Cognac'). The bilingual Spanish-English system also stops halfway: the H2s are English only, and SPIRITS drops to one-language subheads ('AGAVE', 'BRANDY'). Together these make the copy read like four menus stitched together, not one cantina voice.
problems: All 14 items and prices match doc.json exactly (15/15/14/16, 7/8/7/8, 12/11/13, 12/16/18). Nothing is invented. There are no $ signs and every price is a whole number throughout.

House Originals order differs from the draft: the draft has the Brown Butter Old Fashioned first, then the House Daiquiri, and the design swaps them with no note. Nothing is lost, but the change is not logged.

The Manhattan description drops Aromatic Bitters, although it is a sourced component in the draft (doc.json components). The draft description also left it out, but the component row exists. The method words from the draft ('Stirred', 'Shaken') are dropped from every cocktail, which removes the only serve-craft voice the copy had.
The Margarita is the only item with a flavour line ('Bright and citrus-forward.'). This one-off tail breaks the pattern every other item follows.
The serve tags are inconsistent: 'OVER FRESH ICE.' ends with a full stop, while 'COUPE' and 'OVER A LARGE CUBE' do not. The Margarita's tag also sits mid-description, before its flavour line.

The spirit descriptions only repeat the name ('Blanco tequila' under Blanco Tequila, 'Añejo tequila', 'VSOP Cognac'). They dropped the draft's 'poured straight', which was the only extra information and now appears only through the POUR label. Scorecard criterion 12 names exactly this failure.

Bilingual system: every subhead in Cocktails, Beer & Cider and Wine is 'Español · English', but the Spirits subheads are 'AGAVE' and 'BRANDY' in one language, and all four H2s are English only. For a Mexican venue this reads as half-committed.

Venue copy: the wordmark 'CANTINA' is still a placeholder (the designer says so), and the dek 'Cantina & cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' repeats 'Cantina' right under it. Neither the dek nor the wordmark states an item fact, so the tagline check passes. Nothing in the copy says Mexican restaurant beyond the Spanish subheads.

Brut Rosé 13 sits under ESPUMOSO · SPARKLING, not under POR COPA, so a guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or bottle price. The designer correctly flagged this in missing_ingredients, but the page needs a pour label once Rob answers.

Known data gap (Rob asked to fill; not the designer's fault): no beer ABV, brewery or pour size; no wine region, producer or vintage; no spirit brand or añejo age; the cider format is unknown; the Brown Butter Old Fashioned dairy allergen is unconfirmed. Wine and beer therefore cannot meet criterion 8 (grape and region; style and ABV) yet. The missing_ingredients table in proposal.md flags this correctly.

Flow: cocktails, then beer and cider, then wine, then spirits, is correct. The entry through the wordmark and the two-column read are clear, but column 1 ends 160 px lower than column 2 and the agave art takes the remaining space, so Spirits reads as trailing off rather than closing the menu.
fixes: Pick one description grammar for every category (for example ingredients or facts · then a small-caps serve tag with no full stop), and either give every cocktail a one-line flavour tail from known facts or remove 'Bright and citrus-forward.' from the Margarita.

Make the bilingual system complete: add Spanish to the H2s (for example 'Cócteles · Cocktails', 'Cerveza & Sidra', 'Vino', 'Destilados') and restore two-language spirit subheads ('Agave · Agave' can become 'Agave' only if the rule says identical words are shown once; say so in the proposal).

Replace the name-repeating spirit lines with the draft's serve fact ('Served neat', or the draft's 'poured straight') until Rob supplies brand and age, and put Aromatic Bitters back into the Manhattan line with the draft's 'Stirred' and 'Shaken' method words.
Restore the draft order in De la Casa (Brown Butter Old Fashioned, then House Daiquiri), or log the reorder with a reason in proposal.md.

Once Rob answers, add ABV to beer, region to wine, a GLASS or BOTTLE label on Brut Rosé and brand or age on spirits, and replace the placeholder 'CANTINA' wordmark with the venue name so the dek stops repeating it.

lens: missing data: how the design and proposal flag the known gaps (missing_ingredients, dairy allergen, Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle) and whether anything was invented to cover them
top_problem: Nothing was invented and all 14 prices match doc.json (15/15/14/16, 7/8/7/8, 12/11/13, 12/16/18). The Brut Rosé 13 correctly has no glass or bottle label, and Manhattan correctly leaves out the aromatic bitters that are hidden from the public. But the design covers the gaps with silence and filler, not flags. The proposal's missing_ingredients table says the Manhattan has 'none' missing, which is false: the draft flags 'public display of aromatic bitters (needs_input 11)'. The dairy question on the Brown Butter Old Fashioned appears only in the proposal and nowhere on the menu, not even a generic allergen note. Blanco Tequila drops the draft's 'age statement' ask. The spirit lines 'Blanco tequila', 'Añejo tequila' and 'VSOP Cognac' just repeat the item names, and the wine lines 'Dry red wine' and 'Dry white wine' do the same, where the draft's 'poured straight' and grape wording was sourced and read better. So half the list (beer, wine, spirits) reads finished while it lacks brewery, ABV, region, producer and pour size, and nothing on the page shows the reader it is still a placeholder.
fixes: Correct the proposal's missing_ingredients table so the Manhattan row reads 'public display of aromatic bitters (needs_input 11)', the Blanco Tequila row keeps the draft's 'age statement' ask, and Cognac VSOP keeps 'age statement' or notes that VSOP is the stated grade.

Add one generic guest line in brand voice at the foot of the list, such as 'Please tell your server about any allergies', so the unconfirmed dairy in the Brown Butter Old Fashioned is covered without printing an unconfirmed 'contains dairy' claim, and keep the dairy confirmation as an open ask to Rob.

Replace the name-echo spirit and wine descriptions with the draft's sourced wording ('Tequila blanco, poured straight', 'Malbec · dry red', 'Pinot Grigio · dry white', 'Brut rosé · dry sparkling') so no line just repeats its item name.

Keep the Brut Rosé 13 unlabelled, but in the proposal state clearly that its place under the 'Espumoso · Sparkling' subhead, straight after 'Por copa · By the glass', may lead guests to read it as a glass price, and hold the layout until Rob answers.

Add a visible 'draft: brewery / ABV / region / pour size pending' proof-stage marker (or a proposal checklist tied to item ids) so a beer, wine and spirits list with no ABV, region or pour size cannot be signed off as final by mistake.

lens: Ingredient, garnish, glass and serve facts traced to build/draft_doc.json and phg.recipe_versions (gateway log_id 244); description quality; venue fit; description and price layout

The wine lines ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling rosé') are category labels, not descriptions. Half the menu reads as a database printout under a portfolio-grade agave.
verified: Margarita: 'Tequila blanco · fresh lime juice · orange liqueur · agave syrup' matches draft components (beta_margarita); 'lime wheel' matches recipe_versions f06abb74 garnish 'Lime wheel'; 'over fresh ice' matches method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'; 'Bright and citrus-forward.' matches draft desc

problems: Criterion 12 automatic fail: Blanco Tequila / 'Blanco tequila', Añejo Tequila / 'Añejo tequila' and Cognac VSOP / 'VSOP Cognac' repeat the item name, and the three wine lines are category labels
The menu has two voices. The four cocktails get dot-separated ingredient strings, only Margarita gets a flavour sentence, and every other item gets a two-word category label

The serve facts are inconsistent. Manhattan and Daiquiri print the glass (Coupe); Margarita and Old Fashioned print the ice (their Rocks glass is not printed). 'OVER FRESH ICE.' ends with a stray period, and its tasting sentence comes after the serve cap, so the order is ingredients, serve, prose, which appears nowhere else

fixes: Replace the name-echo spirit and wine lines with sourced guest language once Rob supplies brand, age and region. Until then, flag them as missing_ingredients in the draft instead of printing the category name as a description

Pick one serve-fact rule for all four cocktails (glass, or ice with glass) from recipe_versions glassware and method, e.g. Margarita 'rocks · over fresh ice' and Old Fashioned 'rocks · over a large cube', and drop the stray period after FRESH ICE
Give every cocktail the same structure (ingredients, then serve), and either give each one a sourced flavour line or move 'Bright and citrus-forward' before the serve cap
Label Brut Rosé's price as glass or bottle, and add pour sizes to the spirits, beer and cider once Rob answers the open questions

Use one word order for tequila across the menu (e.g. 'blanco tequila' in the Margarita line, matching the item name), and add a dairy note to the Brown Butter Old Fashioned once the allergen is confirmed

lens: description quality and one guest-facing voice (Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City)
top_problem: The menu has no single guest-facing voice. It uses three registers that don't match. The cocktails are dot-separated spec-sheet inventories with small-caps bar-method labels mixed in ("· OVER FRESH ICE.", "· COUPE"). Only the Margarita gets a tasting note ("Bright and citrus-forward."). Everything else prints the draft's taxonomy line, and several of those just repeat the item name: Blanco Tequila / "Blanco tequila", Añejo Tequila / "Añejo tequila", Cognac VSOP / "VSOP Cognac", Dry Cider / "Dry sparkling cider", Brut Rosé / "Dry sparkling rosé", plus the database classes "Dry red wine" and "Dry white wine". The scorecard names this exact pattern as an automatic fail on criterion 12. Every printed fact is sourced, but the menu reads like a data export under a beautiful agave. Checked against the sources: the facts behind the cocktail lines match the draft components and phg.recipe_versions (gateway log 247). Margarita: f06abb74, garnish Lime wheel, method 'Shake with ice and strain over fresh ice'. Manhattan: 9fb77eaa, garnish Cocktail cherry, glass Coupe; the aromatic bitters are hidden correctly per meta.public_components. House Daiquiri: 14d45e57, garnish Lime coin, glass Coupe. Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 7095fd3d, garnish Orange peel, method '...strain over a large cube'. The non-cocktail descriptions are the drafts' menu_description text word for word. Separately, phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b holds a 15th item, "Junmai Ginjo" ("Junmai Ginjo sake."), which is not in draft_doc revision 3. The Coordinator should confirm it was deliberately cut.
fixes: Criterion 12: every description that repeats the name or reads as a database class (the three spirits, rosé, cider, Malbec, Pinot Grigio) should become one short guest-voice line built only from sourced facts. If no facts exist yet, print no description and keep the item flagged missing_ingredients, rather than printing the name back to the guest.

Voice: pick one cocktail format, either all ingredient lists or all lists plus one sourced tasting note. Take the bar-method small caps out of the ingredient line ("OVER FRESH ICE." followed by a full stop and a sentence is the clumsiest line on the page). Tell the designer to give the Coupe / over-ice serve its own quiet position, not the same small-caps style the spirits' POUR price label uses.

Criterion 13: the menu reads as a generic American bar with Spanish subheads. H2s are English-only while the H3s are bilingual, and "Agave" and "Brandy" break the bilingual pattern. Word order is inconsistent ("Tequila blanco" in the Margarita versus "Blanco Tequila" as a name). The venue should decide on a consistent Spanish-first system, and Rob should be asked for mezcal, Mexican beer and more agave-led cocktails for a Mexican restaurant. Designers cannot add these.

Criterion 14: "POUR 12" with no pour size can read as a quantity rather than a price, and Brut Rosé 13 under Espumoso has no glass/bottle label. Keep both labels, but get the pour size and the rosé format from Rob (already in missing_ingredients) before print.

Criterion 12, smaller points: "lime coin" and "cocktail cherry" are back-of-house terms. Keep them, since they are exactly as sourced, but consider whether the guest voice needs a sourced garnish line at all. Also rename the "De la Casa · House Originals" subhead through the venue: a Daiquiri and an Old Fashioned are house versions of classics, not originals.

lens: Venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, IA, including census context and bilingual subheads
top_problem: This reads as a generic American bar list with Spanish labels added, not a Mexican cantina. The Manhattan is placed second among the cocktails, and the list carries Cognac VSOP, an Argentine Malbec, a Czech Pilsner and an Old Fashioned; there is no mezcal, Paloma, Michelada, Mexican lager or food. The Spanish is uneven: all H2s are English only, 'Agave' and 'Brandy' have no Spanish, and 'De la Casa · House Originals' sits over a House Daiquiri, a Cuban classic whose name already says 'House'. Three descriptions only repeat the item name ('Blanco tequila', 'Añejo tequila', 'VSOP Cognac'), which triggers the criterion 12 auto-fail.
fixes: Replace the three name-repeating descriptions and the category-label beer, wine and cider lines, keeping only draft words that add something, and drop the spirit description lines rather than echo the name until Rob supplies brand, region and ABV.

Make the bilingual system complete: Spanish and English on every H2 (e.g. 'Cócteles · Cocktails', 'Vino · Wine', 'Destilados · Spirits'), translate 'Brandy', change 'Espumoso' to the plural 'Espumosos', and relabel 'De la Casa' or move the Daiquiri under Clásicos.

Use one serve label type for all four cocktails: glass (Rocks, Coupe, Coupe, Rocks per recipe_versions f06abb74, 9fb77eaa, 14d45e57, 7095fd3d) or method, and remove the full stop that runs the Margarita label into its tasting note.
Designer note: remove 'POUR' so spirit prices sit 15 px from the name like every other row (it now pushes them to 52 px), and label Brut Rosé 13 as glass or bottle once confirmed.

Coordinator note: put agave first in emphasis (Margarita and agave spirits leading, not the Manhattan), and ask Rob for mezcal, a Mexican lager or michelada, and a real venue name to replace the CANTINA placeholder.

lens: How descriptions, serve labels and prices sit together in preview-letter.png, plus the price-to-item gate
top_problem: The spirits rows fail the description test outright. 'Blanco Tequila / Blanco tequila', 'Añejo Tequila / Añejo tequila' and 'Cognac VSOP / VSOP Cognac' only repeat the item name (the draft text with 'pour' removed). Next to them sits a bare 'POUR' label with no size, so a third of column 2 is a name, its echo and a number. That is an automatic fail on criterion 12 and a serve label that tells the guest nothing.
problems: C12 automatic-fail condition. The three spirit descriptions only restate the name. Source: draft_doc and phg.menu_items.menu_description 'Blanco tequila pour.', 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'VSOP Cognac pour.'. The build strips ' pour' and prints what is left (build.py desc()).

C12. Wine, beer and cider lines are taxonomy class labels, not guest language: 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry sparkling cider'. Rows are verified to phg.menu_items but read as database categories. 'Crisp pale lager', 'Toasty amber lager' and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' are the only appetising lines outside the cocktails.

C14 / C11. The serve-label system is inconsistent. Two cocktails print the glass (Manhattan and House Daiquiri 'COUPE', rv 9fb77eaa and 14d45e57 glassware Coupe). Two print the method (Margarita 'OVER FRESH ICE', rv f06abb74 method; Old Fashioned 'OVER A LARGE CUBE', rv 7095fd3d method), even though both have glassware 'Rocks' on file. The same small-caps style carries two kinds of fact.

C14. Margarita is the only cocktail with a 3-line description. The sourced tasting note 'Bright and citrus-forward.' is tacked on after the serve label 'OVER FRESH ICE.', so the order runs ingredients, serve, tasting note. It reads as an afterthought and is the longest block in the column. Line 1 also ends on a hanging ' ·' separator ('orange liqueur ·').

C14. House Daiquiri breaks as 'house demerara syrup ·' then 'lime coin · COUPE' on line 2. Garnish and glass sit together as a two-word fragment, a near-orphan. The Old Fashioned also puts its serve label on line 2.

C14. 'POUR' labels a price with no pour size (the draft has none, and proposal.md lists it as missing). Brut Rosé 13 sits under 'Espumoso · Sparkling' with no glass or bottle label, while 'Por Copa · By the Glass' covers only the stills. A guest cannot tell whether 13 buys a glass or a bottle. The designer flags this but the print does not solve it.

C14 / C10. In the spirits the price sits after the POUR label (gap 52 px, travel 26% per render_report). Every other row places the price 15 px after the name (4-7%). That makes two price-placement rules on one page. It is under the 40% threshold, so the gate passes, but the rhythm breaks.

C13. It reads as a generic cocktail bar with Spanish subheads. The subheads are correct ('Clásicos', 'De la Casa', 'De Barril', 'Por Copa', 'Espumoso', 'Sidra'). But the lists lead with Czech Pilsner, Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Cognac, and there is no Mexican beer, mezcal or Paloma. The item list is the draft's, but emphasis and naming do nothing to anchor a Mexican cantina beyond the kickers. The 'CANTINA' wordmark is an admitted placeholder.

Content note (not scored as a gate here). phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b holds 'Junmai Ginjo' 12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'). It is absent from the draft doc and from the print. The Content reviewer should confirm whether the draft or the DB list is authoritative.

Verified sources (all pass C11). Margarita: components Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur, Agave Syrup (draft components); garnish 'Lime wheel' and method 'strain over fresh ice' from rv f06abb74. Manhattan: Rye Whiskey, Sweet Vermouth and Cocktail Cherry (draft components); Aromatic Bitters hidden per public_components; glassware Coupe from rv 9fb77eaa. House Daiquiri: White Rum, Fresh Lime Juice, 'house demerara syrup' (the draft description's own wording); 'Lime coin' and Coupe from rv 14d45e57. Brown Butter Old Fashioned: Brown Butter-Washed Bourbon, Demerara Syrup, Aromatic Bitters; 'Orange peel' and 'over a large cube' from rv 7095fd3d. All 14 prices match phg.menu_items.menu_price (gateway log 245). The tagline 'Cantina & cocktail bar · Iowa City, Iowa' states no item fact.
fixes: Replace the three name-echo spirit descriptions with sourced type and serve wording, or print no description and flag missing_ingredients, until Rob supplies brand, age and pour size. Never print a line that only repeats the name.

Make the serve label one kind of fact for every cocktail. Use glassware for all four from recipe_versions ('ROCKS' for Margarita and Old Fashioned, 'COUPE' for Manhattan and Daiquiri), and move method wording into the prose if wanted.

Move 'Bright and citrus-forward.' ahead of the ingredient list, as in the draft description, or drop it, so the Margarita ends on its serve label and fits 2 lines like the others. Fix the hanging ' ·' line ends.
Put the spirits price 15 px after the name, the same rule as every other row, with a size-bearing label once Rob supplies pour sizes. Label Brut Rosé 13 as glass or bottle.

Rewrite the wine and cider class labels ('Dry red wine' and the rest) in the guest voice the beer lines already use, from the draft facts only. Send a note to the designer and Content to reconcile the Junmai Ginjo row and to argue for Mexican-cantina emphasis in the section order.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together on preview-phone.png (1170x4674), plus ingredient accuracy, description quality and fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City

problems: Criterion 12: the spirits descriptions only restate the name ('Blanco tequila', 'Añejo tequila', 'VSOP Cognac'). The wine lines ('Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine') and 'Hop-forward draft IPA' are category wording, not guest language.

Criterion 14, Margarita: the small-caps serve label 'OVER FRESH ICE.' sits mid-paragraph and takes a full stop, then a roman sentence follows on a third line. The label style breaks the sentence, and this is the only description that runs to 3 lines.

Criterion 14, Manhattan: the description breaks at about 60% of the measure ('Rye whiskey · sweet vermouth ·' / 'cocktail cherry · COUPE'), which leaves a ragged, underfilled pair of lines next to the full-measure rows around it.

Criterion 10: the phone row tops fall on mod-8 offsets of 2, 4 and 6 (render_report), and the text ends 34 px above a soil band about 190 css px tall. The phone reads as a letter page poured into one column rather than a designed phone layout.

Add a glass or bottle label to the Brut Rosé price (for example 'COPA 13') once Rob confirms which it is, and show the POR COPA pour label on every wine row.
